questions.question: What describes climate rather than weather?
choices: Long-term patterns and averages of atmospheric conditions
The rainfall during one afternoon
The wind speed at one instant
The temperature on one morning

questions.question: What is the natural greenhouse effect?
choices: Atmospheric gases reflect every form of sunlight back to space
The atmosphere prevents all outgoing radiation
Clouds generate the solar energy reaching Earth
Atmospheric gases absorb and emit infrared radiation, warming the surface and lower atmosphere

questions.question: Which gas is a greenhouse gas?
choices: Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
Oxygen
Argon

questions.question: What is albedo?
choices: The fraction of radiation a surface absorbs only
The fraction of incoming radiation a surface reflects
The speed at which a surface loses heat by conduction
The total infrared radiation emitted by the atmosphere

questions.question: What is a climate proxy?
choices: A forecast of one day's future weather
A direct reading from every ancient thermometer
A model that changes the measured climate
Indirect evidence of past climate

questions.question: Which source can provide evidence of ancient atmospheric composition?
choices: Air bubbles trapped in ice cores
A modern weather forecast for the same location
The current thickness of one cloud
A single afternoon's wind-speed reading

questions.question: What is climate mitigation?
choices: Adjusting only to climate effects after they occur
Recording short-term weather without acting on causes
Reducing the causes or magnitude of climate change
Preparing buildings only for impacts that cannot be reduced

questions.question: Why does burning fossil fuels contribute to recent warming?
choices: It permanently removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
It prevents greenhouse gases from absorbing infrared radiation
It affects temperature only where the fuel is burned
It adds carbon dioxide that changes Earth's energy balance

questions.question: Why does one cold day not disprove a long-term warming trend?
choices: Climate is determined by the most recent temperature alone
A warming trend requires every day to be warmer than all earlier days
Daily weather varies within long-term climate trends
Local temperatures always equal the global average

questions.question: How can melting reflective ice amplify warming?
choices: Darker exposed surfaces absorb more solar energy
Darker exposed surfaces reflect more radiation
Less ice necessarily makes Earth emit no infrared radiation
Melting lowers solar absorption regardless of surface reflectivity

questions.question: Why can warming oceans contribute to sea-level rise?
choices: Warm seawater always occupies less volume
Warmer seawater expands
The water's mass must increase solely from warming
Ocean temperature has no effect on water volume

questions.question: How does melting land-based ice affect sea level?
choices: It removes ocean water through freezing
It has the same direct effect as melting floating sea ice
Land ice never exchanges water with the ocean
It adds water to the ocean

questions.question: Why do scientists use several independent climate measurements?
choices: One local thermometer fully represents every region
Agreement among different evidence sources strengthens conclusions
Only measurements supporting the initial prediction should be used
Agreement proves that no uncertainty remains

questions.question: What is climate adaptation?
choices: Reducing greenhouse-gas emissions as its main definition
Measuring the natural greenhouse effect without changing practices
Adjusting systems to reduce harm from climate impacts
Preventing all natural variations in climate

questions.question: Why are climate projections often given for different emissions scenarios?
choices: Future human activities affect the magnitude of change
The physical laws are different in each scenario
All future emissions pathways have the same outcome
A scenario is a guarantee of one exact future temperature

questions.question: A city's yearly mean temperatures fluctuate but rise over 40 years. Which interpretation is reasonable?
choices: Year-to-year variability can coexist with long-term warming
Every year must be warmer than the one before it
The coldest year invalidates the entire trend
Annual variability means no averages can be calculated

questions.question: Which action is an example of adaptation?
choices: Reducing fossil-fuel use to lower emissions
Capturing carbon dioxide before release
Improving drainage to cope with heavier rainfall
Replacing coal generation to reduce emissions

questions.question: Which observation is stronger evidence of global warming than one hot day?
choices: A high temperature in one classroom
A sustained rise in global average temperature across decades
One afternoon of low humidity
A single local thunderstorm

questions.question: A warming surface melts snow, lowering reflectivity and increasing heat absorption. What kind of feedback is described?
choices: Negative feedback that opposes the initial warming
No feedback because snow is involved
Feedback that creates energy from nothing
Positive feedback that amplifies the initial warming

questions.question: A projection gives a range rather than one exact temperature. What is the appropriate interpretation?
choices: It proves all temperatures are equally likely
It means measurements have no value
It reflects uncertainty and differing possible conditions
It guarantees the lowest value will occur
